title: Check yourself: best practices for custom exceptions

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A reporting library's `Exporter.export()` throws `TemplateMissingException` and `RenderTimeoutException`, two unchecked exceptions that each extend `RuntimeException` directly. Your service calls it and catches both by name. Version 3 adds a third, `QuotaExceededException`, also extending `RuntimeException` directly, and your build picks version 3 up. An export then runs over its quota. What happens?

options.text: It compiles, and the quota failure escapes both catch blocks at run time, since neither block's type is a supertype of the new exception
options.says: the ATM run: AccountFrozenException, added as an unrelated unchecked exception, went past both catch blocks and ended the program

options.text: It compiles, and the quota failure lands in the nearer of the two catch blocks, since both blocks catch a subclass of RuntimeException
options.says: a catch block takes only its own type and its subclasses; the new exception is a sibling of both, so it passes them, as AccountFrozenException did

options.text: It fails to compile at the export() call, since that call can now throw an exception that nothing around it catches or declares
options.says: only checked exceptions must be caught or declared; with unchecked ones the ATM compiled, and the new exception escaped at run time

options.text: It fails to compile at the two catch blocks, since three exceptions from one call must be caught through a shared superclass
options.says: there is no such rule; the existing catch blocks stay valid, and the unchecked ATM compiled against the next release

origin.section: Give a Module One Base Exception, So Each Caller Chooses How Finely It Catches

questions.stem: A gym's booking API answers IllegalArgumentException with 400, IllegalStateException with 409, and anything else with 500. `ClassSchedule.book(memberId, classId)` is called for a class whose booking window opens tomorrow at 06:00. What should it throw?

options.text: IllegalStateException, since nothing in the call is wrong and only its timing stops the booking
options.says: the argument is fine but the moment is wrong, like the closed booking that should answer 409

options.text: IllegalArgumentException, since the classId in the call can't be booked at that time
options.says: a 400 tells the client to change a request that was right; the closed booking reported as IllegalArgumentException is the page's example of that

options.text: A new BookingNotOpenException extending RuntimeException, since a class of its own names the problem exactly
options.says: the existing handler doesn't know the new class and answers 500, as SeatNotFoundException did

options.text: A new BookingNotOpenException extending IllegalArgumentException, since a class of its own still reaches the existing handler
options.says: it reaches the handler as a 400, which tells the client its request is wrong; a subclass keeps its parent's meaning, so the parent has to fit

origin.section: Throw IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException or UnsupportedOperationException When They Already Mean the Error

questions.stem: A payout passes through `BankClient`, `PayoutService` and `PayoutJob`. `BankClient` catches an IOException, logs it at SEVERE and rethrows it. `PayoutService` wraps it in a PayoutException with the IOException as the cause, logs that at SEVERE and rethrows it. `PayoutJob` catches it, logs it at SEVERE and schedules a retry. Monitoring raises one alert per SEVERE record. One payout fails once. What does on-call get?

options.text: Three alerts, each showing the IOException in its stack trace, since each of the three log calls writes its own record
options.says: the order-lookup run: three SEVERE records and 24 lines, with 'connection reset' three times, for one SQLException

options.text: Three alerts, and only the first shows the IOException, since a wrapper's stack trace replaces the one of its cause
options.says: a wrapper made with the cause prints it under 'Caused by', so the last two records show the IOException as well

options.text: One alert, holding all three messages, since the logger merges records that carry the same exception
options.says: java.util.logging writes each log call as its own record; the run shows three separate SEVERE records

options.text: One alert, from BankClient only, since an exception already written to the log is skipped by later log calls
options.says: nothing marks an exception as logged; each layer's log call writes a record, which is why only the handling layer should log

origin.section: Log an Exception Where It Is Handled, Never Where It Is Rethrown

questions.stem: A web layer maps payment failures with `int status = switch (e.code()) { case CARD_DECLINED -> 402; case INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS -> 422; default -> 500; };`. A developer adds `RISK_REVIEW` to the `ErrorCode` enum, throws it for held payments, and ships. What does a client get for a held payment?

options.text: The client gets a 500, since a constant that no case names is taken by the default branch
options.says: with a default the switch is exhaustive for the compiler, so the new constant compiles and falls to 500

options.text: The client gets a 422, since a constant that no case names falls to the case written just above the default branch
options.says: arrow cases don't fall through; an enum switch matches by constant, and an unnamed one goes to the default branch

options.text: No build ships, since the switch must name every constant even when it has a default branch
options.says: that compile error happens only when the switch expression has no default; with one, nothing stops the build

options.text: No build ships, since the enum can't gain a constant while a switch with a default branch names the others
options.says: an enum compiles regardless of the switches over it; a missing case is reported at the switch, and only without a default

origin.section: Clients Branch on an Error Code, Never on the Message

concepts: A switch expression over the error-code enum with no default stops compiling when a constant is added; with a default, the new code falls to the fallback.
Logging and rethrowing at each layer writes one record per layer for a single failure, multiplying alerts.
IllegalArgumentException means the argument is wrong whatever the state; IllegalStateException means the argument is fine but the moment is wrong, and the choice decides what the client is told.
A new unchecked leaf escapes a caller that catches the module's exceptions only by name; the code still compiles.
